# 11QMelchizedek Column 2 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** 11Q13 (Cave 11), Col. 2 | **Condition:** fragmentary; main surviving column with ~26 partially preserved lines

---

**2:1** [...And regarding what] He declared: "In [this] jubilee year, [each of you shall return to his own land" (Lev 25:13);

**2:2** and regarding what] He declared: "Eve[ry] creditor must cancel [what he has loaned to his neighbor; he must not demand payment from his neighbor or his brother, for]

**2:3** God's release [has been announced]" (Deut 15:2).

**2:4** [The mean]ing of this for the end times concerns the captives, about whom

**2:5** He declared: "To announce freedom to the captives" (Isa 61:1). This means that He will entrust them to the Sons of Heaven and to Melchizedek's inheritance,

**2:6** [for He will re]store them. And he will announce their freedom, releasing them from [the burden of] all their sins.

**2:7** And this will [come about] during the first week of the jubilee following the ni[ne] jubilees.

**2:8** And the Day of [Atone]ment marks the e[nd of the] tenth [jub]ilee,

**2:9** when atonement will be made for all the Children of [Light and] for the people who belong to Mel[chi]zedek.

**2:10** [...over the]m [...] for

**2:11** that is the appointed time of "the year of grace" for Melchizedek (Isa 61:2), and [for his] arm[ies,

**2:12** the nati]on of God's holy ones, who carry out the rule of justice, as it is written

**2:13** about him in the psalms of David, who said: "God has taken his place in the heavenly [council];

**2:14** among the divine beings he renders judgment" (Ps 82:1). And about him it was said: "[Let the assembly of the nations]

**2:15** gather before him on high; God above will [j]udge the nations" (Ps 7:8–9).

**2:16** As for what was sa[id: "How long will you] render unjust verdicts and sh[ow]

**2:17** favoritism to the wicked? [Se]lah" (Ps 82:2) —

**2:18** this refers to Belial and the spirits who follow him, who [...]

**2:19** by tur[ning] away from God's commands [to do evil].

**2:20** And Melchizedek will carry out God's veng[eance] and judgment [against Be]lial and against all the [spirits] who [follow] him.

**2:21** And all the [eternal] heavenly beings will come to his aid. [This] is what [He meant]:

**2:22** all the sons of Mi[ght and ...] the [m]ission of Melchizedek.

**2:23** And [regarding what He declared]: "How beautiful on the mountains are the feet of the messen[ger who]

**2:24** announces peace, the messen[ger of good news who announces salva]tion, who says to Zion: 'Your God [is king]'" (Isa 52:7).

**2:25** This means: the mountains stand for the pro[phets ...] and the messenger is the one anoin[ted by the Spir]it,

**2:26** the one Dan[iel] spoke of: ["Until an anointed ruler comes" (Dan 9:25) ...]

---

*PNEUMA notes: This dynamic translation prioritizes clarity and impact for modern readers while preserving the eschatological urgency of the Qumran pesher. Melchizedek emerges here as a transcendent heavenly judge — not the Genesis 14 priest-king but a cosmic figure who will execute God's final vengeance against Belial (Satan) and liberate the captive faithful. The pesher technique reads biblical texts as encrypted prophecies fulfilled in the sect's own time: the jubilee framework (10 jubilees = 490 years) parallels Daniel's "seventy weeks." The identification of Melchizedek with "God" (Elohim) in Psalm 82 is striking — he stands in God's own council and judges the nations. "Children of Light" is the community's self-designation; "Sons of Heaven" refers to angelic allies. The anointed messenger of line 25 may be the Teacher of Righteousness or a prophetic forerunner.*
